aperture-duty-cycle.toml:
# Aperture duty-cycle demonstrator (ground segment & operations).
#
# How a contact plan divides a pool of steerable apertures between navigation
# (ranging / tracking) and communications (data), and what each session loses when
# more sessions are active than there are apertures.
#
# THE ARBITRATION POLICY IS AN INPUT. A duty figure is only meaningful relative to
# a stated rule for who wins the aperture, so the policy is declared here, echoed
# back in the report with its full definition, and named in the one-line summary.
#   navigation-priority       (default) navigation preempts communications
#   communications-priority             communications preempts navigation
#   first-come-first-served             non-preemptive; the holder keeps the aperture
#
# Re-run with `apertures = 1` to see the one-aperture time-share: on this plan
# navigation is served in full either way and the whole contention loss lands on
# the communications sessions.
#
# HONEST SCOPE: MODELLED scheduling arithmetic over the supplied windows. No slew /
# retune / changeover time is charged when an aperture changes service or session;
# no data volume, buffer state, energy budget or link closure enters the decision;
# and the contact windows are inputs -- their geometry is whatever produced them
# (the `passes` scenario emits the same aos_s / los_s vocabulary). Not a
# ground-segment scheduling product.
# Run:  kshana scenarios/aperture-duty-cycle.toml
kind = "aperture-duty-cycle"

apertures = 2
arbitration = "navigation-priority"

# The reporting horizon defaults to the plan envelope (earliest aos_s -> latest
# los_s), which is what sets the duty denominator (apertures * horizon_s). Override
# it to score the plan over a fixed operational day instead:
#   horizon_start_s = 0.0
#   horizon_end_s = 86400.0

# The contact plan. ILLUSTRATIVE: three navigation sessions and three
# communications sessions over a 9 000 s envelope, each navigation session
# overlapping a communications one.

service = "navigation"

araim-gps-galileo.toml:
# Dual-constellation ARAIM availability: GPS + Galileo evaluated with the advanced
# ARAIM engine, including the constellation-wide fault hypothesis (`araim_dual`).
#
# Unlike `integrity-raim.toml` (single-constellation solution-separation RAIM), this
# runs `araim_dual_raim` at every epoch over a combined GPS + Galileo geometry: the
# fault-free, single-satellite, AND per-constellation fault hypotheses all feed one
# MHSS integrity-risk budget (P_HMI). The primary constellation is fault group 0 and
# each `[[constellations]]` entry the next group.
#
# Constellation-fault-robust integrity (staying safe even if an entire constellation
# fails) is the demanding mode: under the constellation-fault hypothesis the residual
# constellation must carry the fix alone, so it always costs availability relative to
# pooling. How much depends on the sky. On the real 2026-06-07 GPS + Galileo catalogue,
# evaluated at one common epoch, it still reaches 0.990 at a 12 m VAL against 1.000
# pooled (tests/araim_dual_real_data.rs) — two full constellations can carry it; a
# depleted one is where a third constellation or SBAS augmentation earns its place.
# The numerically exact EU ARAIM TN Table A-3 reproduction is an external follow-on
# (docs/ARAIM_REFERENCE.md).
kind = "integrity"

mask_deg = 5.0
sigma_uere_m = 0.75   # ISM σ_URA (dual-frequency, m)
p_fa = 1.0e-5         # false-alarm / continuity budget
p_md = 1.0e-3
al_h_m = 40.0         # horizontal alert limit (APV-I)
al_v_m = 50.0         # vertical alert limit (APV-I)
araim_dual = true     # advanced dual-/multi-constellation ARAIM
p_hmi = 1.0e-7        # per-axis integrity-risk budget

[time]
step_s = 300.0
duration_s = 43200.0  # 12 h

[user]
altitude_km = 0.4
inclination_deg = 45.0
raan_deg = 10.0
u0_deg = 0.0

[constellation]       # GPS-like Walker 24/6/1
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

[[constellations]]    # Galileo-like Walker 24/3/1
altitude_km = 23222.0
inclination_deg = 56.0
planes = 3
sats_per_plane = 8
phasing_f = 1.0
araim-reference-check.toml:
# The engine's ARAIM protection levels against the WG-C subgroup's OWN worked examples.
#
# This is an EXTERNAL check, not a self-test: two published certification reference vectors
# are committed as fixtures, each carrying its retrieval URL, retrieval date, source-file
# SHA-256 and page number, and the engine's numbers are run against them at the tolerance
# (TOL_PL = 5e-2 m) those documents themselves state.
#
#   * Reference Airborne Algorithm Description Document v3.1 (2019), Appendix D — internally
#     self-consistent, and the acceptance vector.
#   * Milestone 3 Report (2016), Annex A section A.IX — the statement the research
#     bibliographies cite.
#
# Every published input (the 10-satellite 2-constellation geometry matrix, the C_int and
# C_acc variance diagonals, b_nom, P_sat, P_const and the LPV-200 constant set) and every
# published output (VPL, HPL, EMT, sigma_v_acc, K_fa_3, and each constellation-fault mode's
# sigma_3, sigma_ss_3 and b_3) is reported beside the engine's own number and their absolute
# difference. A transcribed figure is labelled `published` so it can never be mistaken for a
# computed one.
#
# The protection-level equation is NOT re-solved here. The reference's mode list is handed
# to the engine's existing raim::araim_protection_level / araim_integrity_risk, so the
# bisection and the Gaussian-tail algebra under test are the engine's own; only the geometry,
# the sub-solutions, the detection thresholds and the published budget split are built for it.
#
# RESULT against the 2019 vector: VPL 18.2926 m vs 18.3 m published, HPL 13.4063 m vs
# 13.45 m, EMT 7.2997 m vs 7.2998 m, sigma_v_acc 1.3694 m vs 1.3694 m, and all six published
# intermediates to within half a unit in their last printed decimal.
#
# The 2016 vector carries two internal defects the report STATES rather than hides — a sign
# typo in row 3 of G, and a K_fa_3 evaluated at 57 fault modes while the document states
# N_fault_max = 1 (12 modes). Its geometry intermediates reproduce exactly; its protection
# levels are reported as measured discrepancies and excluded from the acceptance figure.
# The tolerance is never widened to absorb them.
#
# SCOPE: only N_fault_max = 1 (single-satellite and single-constellation fault modes) is
# implemented, and a case whose priors require simultaneous multi-event fault subsets is
# REFUSED rather than silently truncated. Fault detection, exclusion, the chi-square
# consistency check and the double-counting re-allocation step are out of scope. This
# reproduces a published reference algorithm's worked example — it is not a certification,
# an airworthiness artefact, or an approval.
#
# Omit `vector` to run both; set it to select one.

kind = "araim-reference-check"

automotive-urban-canyon.toml:
# Road vehicle through an urban canyon: GNSS/INS dead-reckoning across an underpass and
# a roadside jammer, against a lane-level budget.
#
# The mission question a driver-assistance or automated-driving team asks: a car's
# Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) receiver loses the sky under an overpass and
# then again near a roadside jammer (a low-power in-vehicle "privacy" jammer on a
# neighbouring vehicle is the common case). How long does the fused GNSS/inertial
# navigation system (INS) solution stay inside half a lane? The 1.5 m threshold is half
# a 3.5 m lane less a margin, a budget chosen here, not a standard's figure.
#
# The pack is `gnss-ins`: a three-axis strapdown navigator disciplined by a 15-state
# error-state extended Kalman filter (EKF), then coasting through the outages. The
# GNSS timeline: open sky for 60 s, a 15 s underpass, 45 s of open sky, then 60 s
# near the jammer.
#
# The pack has two fixed slots named `imu_quantum` and `imu_classical`. Here
# `imu_quantum` carries the BETTER unit, a tactical-grade comparator, and
# `imu_classical` carries an automotive MEMS (micro-electro-mechanical system) unit.
# Nothing quantum is modelled in this file. Both use the representative class
# coefficients from the engine's grade table (Groves 2013, Table 4.1 band; the same
# figures as `imu_grade` in `ins-trn-coast`), NOT a datasheet for any part:
#   - tactical: accelerometer bias 300 ug = 2.94e-3 m/s^2, gyro bias 1 deg/h =
#     4.848e-6 rad/s;
#   - industrial (automotive MEMS sits in this band): accelerometer bias 3000 ug =
#     2.94e-2 m/s^2, gyro bias 20 deg/h = 9.696e-5 rad/s, accelerometer scale factor
#     2000 ppm.
#
# Honest scope (inherited from the `gnss-ins` pack): loosely coupled, the pack's single
# deterministic driving profile (a forward-acceleration and yaw square wave), not a
# recorded drive; no odometer or wheel-speed aiding (the engine has none), no
# multipath model, and constant biases, which the filter can learn while GNSS is up,
# so the coast is a best case for these classes. MODELLED: every figure is modelled.
kind = "gnss-ins"
seed = 7
threshold_m = 1.5
fix_interval_s = 1.0
sigma_pos_m = 1.0
sigma_vel_mps = 0.05
lat_deg = 48.137
lon_deg = 11.575
alt_m = 520.0

[time]
step_s = 0.1
duration_s = 180.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 60.0,  state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 60.0,  t1 = 75.0,  state = "denied" },
  { t0 = 75.0,  t1 = 120.0, state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 120.0, t1 = 180.0, state = "denied" },
]

[imu_quantum]
id = "tactical-imu"
provenance = "Tactical-grade class (Groves 2013 Table 4.1 band, engine grade table): accel bias 300 ug = 2.94e-3 m/s^2, gyro bias 1 deg/h = 4.848e-6 rad/s; signs chosen"
accel_bias = [2.94e-3, -2.94e-3, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [0.0, 0.0, 4.848e-6]

[imu_quantum.filter_prior]
sigma_accel_bias = 2.94e-3
sigma_gyro_bias = 4.848e-6

[imu_classical]
id = "automotive-mems"
provenance = "Industrial-grade class, where automotive MEMS units sit (Groves 2013 Table 4.1 band, engine grade table): accel bias 3000 ug = 2.94e-2 m/s^2, gyro bias 20 deg/h = 9.696e-5 rad/s; signs chosen"
accel_bias = [2.94e-2, -2.94e-2, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [9.696e-5, -9.696e-5, 9.696e-5]

[imu_classical.filter_prior]
sigma_accel_bias = 2.94e-2
sigma_gyro_bias = 9.696e-5

# The class's accelerometer scale-factor error (2000 ppm) layered on the constant bias.
[imu_classical.error_model]
scale_accel_ppm = [2000.0, 2000.0, 2000.0]
cislunar-arc-recovery.toml:
# Independent-estimator test of the cislunar arc-length observability threshold (R6, paper B).
#
# Paper B's threshold is a RANK read on an observability matrix assembled from the ANALYTIC
# range Jacobian rows and the ANALYTIC variational state-transition matrix, and its
# square-root-information-filter cross-check folds those same rows. The paper says so: that
# is a consistency check between two numerical machines, not corroboration. This scenario is
# the missing arbiter — a batch least-squares estimator that actually RECOVERS the chief's
# initial state from simulated measurements, with the measurement partials taken as CENTRAL
# FINITE DIFFERENCES of the composed forward model.
#
# It calls no analytic Jacobian row, no variational STM, no singular-value or eigen
# decomposition, no rank tolerance and no square-root information filter. That is enforced,
# not promised: a source-text guard in tests/cislunar_arc_recovery_reference.rs fails if any
# of them appears. The dynamics (the same RK4 CR3BP flow), the initial conditions (the same
# differential-corrected constellation), the scalar observable and the epoch grid ARE shared,
# deliberately and by name, in the emitted `independence` block — two analyses of one
# physical problem must agree about the physics to be comparable.
#
# Two criteria, each swept over five decades of its own bound:
#   * NOISE-FREE RECOVERY — every seeded trial's final state error at most recovery_factor
#     times its a-priori displacement. The rank analogue, with no singular-value tolerance
#     anywhere in it.
#   * MONTE-CARLO ESTIMABILITY — measured RMS position error over a seeded noise ensemble
#     below a stated bound. The estimability analogue, measured rather than predicted.
#
# MEASURED on the published planar DRO grid: the estimator recovers the four-state from
# 0.782609 h against the rank criterion's 2.086957 h at rel_tol 1e-6, a ratio of 0.375 — so
# the rank threshold is NOT corroborated as a recoverability boundary. The measured
# estimability boundary lands in the same grid cell as the formal one, 5.739130 h, and the
# measured error curve reproduces the formal 1-sigma over 21 arc lengths to a geometric-mean
# ratio of 0.98.
#
# MODELLED: the constellation design, the epoch grid, the single tracked link, the
# displacement magnitude, the measurement sigma and the two stated bounds.
# Not a certified navigation-performance product.

kind = "cislunar-arc-recovery"
cislunar-observability.toml:
# Planar cislunar constellation observability over a tracking arc (P6).
#
# A small four-spacecraft near-DRO planar constellation near the Moon is tracked by
# inter-satellite ranging. The scenario answers the batch-estimator question: how much of a
# spacecraft's four-state [x, y, xdot, ydot] does the arc actually make observable, and how
# does that grow with arc length? It assembles the observability structure from the crate's
# finite-difference-validated CR3BP variational STM (src/cr3bp.rs) and the analytic
# inter-satellite range / range-rate Jacobians (src/intersat_range.rs), and emits:
#   1. the rank-vs-arc-length table for a single range-only link -- instantaneously rank-1,
#      growing toward the full four-state as the arc lengthens (P6 Table 1);
#   2. the observability-Gramian eigen-spectrum + condition number over the arc; and
#   3. the range-only vs range+range-rate instantaneous-rank comparison (the Doppler design
#      lever) plus range-only-singular / range+rate-defined GDOP reporting.
# (src/cislunar_observability.rs, src/observability_gramian.rs)
#
# Honesty: MODELLED. VALIDATED core -- the observable RANK is a rank-revealing
# singular-value threshold cross-checked against the Gramian eigen-rank; the eigen-spectrum
# obeys the spectral invariants (trace = sum eig, det = prod eig, Frobenius^2 = sum eig^2);
# the variational STM is the finite-difference-validated CR3BP STM; the range / range-rate
# Jacobian rows are finite-difference-validated analytic partials (cross-checked against the
# crate's 3-D range-rate observable); a rank-deficient snapshot is flagged GDOP-undefined
# (fim condition = inf), never a bogus finite value -- the same singular-geometry guard
# pvt::solve_spp applies. MODELLED -- the four near-DRO planar initial conditions (a
# differential-corrected DRO seeder is a follow-on) and the specific rank progression they
# produce. Not a certified navigation-performance product.
kind = "cislunar-observability"

# Every field is optional and shown at its default. Uncomment to override.
# mu        = 0.012150585609624   # Earth-Moon mass ratio
# arc_hours = 6.0                 # tracking-arc length (hours)
# epochs    = 24                  # epochs sampled along the arc
# steps     = 2000                # RK4 sub-steps per STM propagation
# rel_tol   = 1.0e-6              # singular-value threshold for the observable-rank read

combined-altpnt.toml:
# Combined gravity + magnetic + terrain GPS-denied navigator — fused alt-PNT.
#
# The capstone alternative-PNT demo: a vehicle flying with no GNSS takes THREE scalar
# measurements at each waypoint — gravity anomaly (mGal), magnetic-anomaly total intensity
# (nT), and ground elevation (m). For a candidate constant drift offset the joint likelihood
# is the PRODUCT of the three field likelihoods, so the information adds: the joint posterior
# is sharper (a lower CRLB) than any single field. The demo shows a bounded error under 500 m
# over the outage that is never worse than the best single channel — exactly why sensor fusion
# is the path where any one weak field alone would struggle.
#
# Consumed by `kshana::altpnt::terrain::run_combined_altpnt` (and its unit tests), dispatched
# as `kind = "combined-altpnt"`. The gravity field is a low-degree spherical-harmonic trend +
# synthetic mascons; the magnetic channel is the smooth IGRF-14 main field minus its regional
# mean PLUS synthetic crustal-anomaly mascons (the IGRF main field alone is too smooth to
# localise — the real crustal map is a follow-on, see docs/CAPABILITY.md); the terrain channel
# is the self-contained synthetic DEM. Recovery is checked against the INDEPENDENTLY injected
# drift, never any field's own value (non-circular).
#
# NOTE: every top-level scalar key precedes the `[[...]]` array-of-tables blocks — a scalar
# after an array-of-table would be absorbed into that table by TOML.
kind = "combined-altpnt"

# Track + drift + search (shared across the three channels).
start_lat_deg = 12.05
start_lon_deg = 20.05
step_lat_deg = 0.004
step_lon_deg = 0.003
waypoints = 60

drift_lat_deg = 0.5
drift_lon_deg = -0.4

search_half_deg = 0.8
search_step_deg = 0.08
refine_stages = 3
refine_factor = 8.0
noise_seed = 1

# ---- Gravity channel ----
# Each single-channel σ is set so that channel ALONE recovers only to ~600–900 m (well above
# the ~140 m grid floor), making the fusion gain visible: the three-channel product collapses
# to ~250 m (< 500 m), no worse than the best single channel.
nmax = 3
gravity_sigma_mgal = 3.0

# ---- Magnetic channel (IGRF main field + synthetic crustal anomaly mascons, nT) ----
igrf_year = 2025.0
igrf_alt_km = 0.0
magnetic_sigma_nt = 30.0

# ---- Terrain channel (synthetic DEM) ----
dem_seed = 1
terrain_sigma_m = 40.0

# Low-degree anomalous gravity coefficients (the regional trend).
[[coeffs]]
n = 2
m = 0
cbar = 6.0e-6
sbar = 0.0

[[coeffs]]
n = 3
m = 1
cbar = 3.0e-6
sbar = 2.0e-6

# Localized gravity mascons (mGal) the track crosses.
[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.18
lon_deg = 20.16
amp_mgal = 45.0
sigma_deg = 0.05

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.26
lon_deg = 20.22
amp_mgal = -38.0
sigma_deg = 0.045

# Synthetic crustal magnetic-anomaly mascons (nT) the track crosses.
[[magnetic_mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.20
lon_deg = 20.18
amp_mgal = 250.0
sigma_deg = 0.05

[[magnetic_mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.24
lon_deg = 20.20
amp_mgal = -200.0
sigma_deg = 0.045
conflict-resilience.toml:
# Layered-PNT conflict resilience (paper P7).
#
# A contested-environment user fields four RF PNT layers that all ride the same band
# and therefore share the jamming/spoofing denial vector — the fragile, correlated
# case. The scenario reports:
#   * total-loss probability vs threat intensity (Monte-Carlo vs the closed-form
#     independent product it converges to),
#   * the ~7x layered-vs-single-layer resilience ratio under the independence
#     assumption,
#   * how that ~7x collapses toward 1 as the denial correlation rises (a one-factor
#     Gaussian copula) — correlation defeats layering, and
#   * a §4.2 per-vector usable-PNT survival breakdown: for each named threat vector
#     (jamming/spoofing/kinetic/cyber) acting alone, the graceful-degradation curve
#     S_v(x) = 1 - Prod_i (1 - a_i*(1 - clamp(susceptibility_i,v * x, 0, 1))). Jamming
#     is the sharpest vector for this correlated-RF stack.
#
# Every per-layer magnitude is a MODELLED input with provenance; see
# src/conflict_threat_params.rs for the sourced [min, nominal, max] priors and the

earth-gnss-lunar.toml:
# Earth-GNSS reception at lunar distance.
#
# A GNSS constellation is built to serve users under it. A receiver near the Moon is
# roughly fifteen times the orbital radius away, outside that service volume entirely, and
# three facts decide whether it can hear anything at all:
#
#   1. THE EARTH BLOCKS THE BORESIGHT. From 26,560 km the Earth subtends a half-angle of
#      about 13.9 deg. Any ray that reaches the Moon must therefore leave the transmitter
#      at least that far off nadir — the peak of the beam is geometrically unavailable
#      before a single dB is computed.
#   2. WHAT IS LEFT IS THE EDGE OF THE MAIN LOBE AND THE SIDELOBES. The usable rays sit in
#      a thin annulus just outside the limb, where the transmit gain is already falling.
#      This is the regime the LuGRE payload operated in when it tracked GNSS at the Moon
#      in 2025.
#   3. THE PATH LOSS IS ABOUT 208 dB AT L1 — some 25 dB more than a terrestrial user pays.
#      The budget closes only with a high-gain receiving antenna, and it closes narrowly.
#
# The run reports one row per satellite (off-boresight angle, Earth occultation, range,
# path loss, transmit gain at that angle, received power, C/N0) and then aggregates only
# the links that clear the tracking threshold.
#
# READ THE CONDITIONING, NOT JUST THE COUNT
# Every satellite the receiver can hear lies inside a cone a couple of degrees wide, so the
# lines of sight are nearly parallel and the dilution of precision is enormous. That is not
# a defect of the model; it is the defining property of the layer. An Earth-GNSS fix at
# lunar distance is a TIMING-grade observation far more than a position-grade one, and the
# report prints the DOP rather than quietly omitting it.
#
# WHAT IS MODELLED, AND WHY IT IS NOT VALIDATED
# The transmit gain at angle is a uniformly illuminated circular aperture — an Airy
# pattern. A real GPS L1 antenna is a twelve-element helical array whose measured pattern
# has a shaped main lobe, deliberately peaked off-boresight to even out power across the
# Earth disc, and sidelobes that are not Airy at all. Measured patterns are published; they
# are not vendored in this repository, so they are not used here. Orderings and orders of
# magnitude are meaningful. The dB of any single satellite is not.
#
# Also absent, and every one of these makes the budget OPTIMISTIC: no ionospheric or
# tropospheric loss on the limb-grazing rays (which do clip the upper atmosphere at small
# clearance angles), no polarisation mismatch, no pointing loss, no receiver implementation
# loss, and a spherical Earth with no refractive extension of the occultation.
#
# Upgrading this to Validated needs two things the repository does not hold: a measured
# transmit pattern, and LuGRE normal points to check against. Neither is invented here.
#
# The Moon position is an INPUT — a range and an inertial direction — not an ephemeris
# lookup. What is under test is the link and the beam geometry; the engine models the lunar
# ephemeris elsewhere and coupling them would only obscure which part is being checked.

kind = "earth-gnss-lunar"

# The constellation: a 24-satellite Walker at GPS altitude and inclination.
altitude_km = 20180.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 2.0
epoch_s = 0.0

# The receiver, at the mean lunar distance along the inertial x-axis.
receiver_range_m = 384400000.0
receiver_ra_deg = 0.0
receiver_dec_deg = 0.0

# Transmitter: about 27 W into an aperture sized so the boresight gain lands near the
# 13 dBi a GPS L1 antenna is usually quoted at.
tx_power_dbw = 13.4
tx_diameter_m = 0.35
tx_efficiency = 0.6
freq_hz = 1575420000.0

# Receiver: a modest high-gain lunar antenna and a room-temperature system.
rx_gain_dbi = 12.0
system_temp_k = 290.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

# Earth-observation payload footprint & coverage demonstrator (SMAD space triangle).

# Turns an orbit altitude + sensor field of view into the Earth angular radius,
# swath width, nadir ground sample distance, maximum off-nadir access, circular
# period and equatorial ground-track spacing (with a contiguous-coverage flag).
#
# HONEST SCOPE: MODELLED spherical-Earth geometry only -- no radiometry / MTF /
# atmosphere / pointing-jitter / sun-glint model; ground-track spacing is the
# simple nodal R_e*omega*T (no J2 nodal regression).

ephemeris.toml:
kind = "ephemeris"

# Ephemeris & ground track — "where is the satellite right now".
#
# Propagate the ISS (ZARYA) for one revolution and emit, at every 30 s step: the
# inertial TEME and GCRS (≈ J2000) state (position AND velocity), the Earth-fixed
# ITRF/ECEF position, the WGS-84 sub-satellite point (latitude / longitude /
# altitude — the ground track drawn in the chart), and the topocentric azimuth /
# elevation / range and range-rate (the geometric Doppler) seen from a ground
# station. The frame chain is the one validated to the millimetre against the
# published Vallado vectors; the velocity is validated against the official AIAA
# tcppver vectors.
#
# A TLE's epoch is its own (UTC); the ground track therefore starts at the TLE
# epoch. Swap in any current TLE (e.g. from CelesTrak) to track a live satellite.
tle = """
1 25544U 98067A   20045.18587073  .00000950  00000-0  25302-4 0  9990
2 25544  51.6443 242.0161 0004885 264.6060 207.3845 15.49165514212791
"""

duration_s = 16740.0   # ~three ISS revolutions

# arcsecond / few-hundred-metre longitude shift in the ground track); xp_arcsec /
# yp_arcsec are the IERS polar-motion pole coordinates. Leave at 0 for a quick run,
# or supply IERS values.
dut1_s = 0.0
xp_arcsec = 0.0
yp_arcsec = 0.0

# Drives the az / el / range and the range-rate / Doppler columns.
[station]
lat_deg = 49.8707
lon_deg = 8.6217
alt_m = 144.0

gnss-ins.toml:
# Loosely-coupled GNSS/INS: the three-axis strapdown navigator disciplined by a
# 15-state error-state EKF, then coasting through a 60 s GNSS outage. Unlike the
# `inertial` pack (a 1-DOF scalar dead-reckoner with a truth-snap reset at every
# fix), this runs the genuine closed-loop filter: it learns from noisy fixes while
# GNSS is up and coasts on the corrected state during the gap. The reported error
# is the real horizontal residual against truth; each sensor also carries its
# open-loop free-INS RMS so the filter's value is explicit.
#
# Honest framing: loosely-coupled, a single deterministic driving trajectory, a
# flat-Earth tangent-plane INS<->GNSS comparison. The lower-bias (quantum-grade)
# sensor has the better unaided coast. Both biases here are constant and noise-free,
# so the filter learns them while GNSS is up and the fused coast is a best case; a
# bias that keeps drifting is what ends a real one (see small-uas-jammed-nav.toml).
# Revised in 0.27.3: a sign error in the filter's gyro-bias coupling had put a floor
# of tens of metres under the fused outage error; see the CHANGELOG.
kind = "gnss-ins"
seed = 7
threshold_m = 50.0
fix_interval_s = 1.0
sigma_pos_m = 1.0
sigma_vel_mps = 0.05
lat_deg = 45.0
lon_deg = -57.3
alt_m = 50.0

[time]
step_s = 0.1
duration_s = 160.0

[gnss]
windows = [
  { t0 = 0.0,   t1 = 100.0, state = "nominal" },
  { t0 = 100.0, t1 = 160.0, state = "denied" },
]

[imu_quantum]
id = "cold-atom-imu"
provenance = "Quantum-grade inertial unit: low residual accelerometer/gyro bias (cold-atom-class); the better unaided coast"
accel_bias = [0.015, 0.0, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [0.0, 0.0, 5.0e-5]

[imu_classical]
id = "tactical-imu"
provenance = "Tactical-grade MEMS/quartz inertial unit: larger residual bias; the free-running INS diverges much faster"
accel_bias = [0.03, -0.02, 0.0]
gyro_bias = [0.0, 0.0, 1.0e-4]

# Optional: layer the full deterministic IMU error chain on top of the constant
# biases above. Every field defaults to zero, so omitting this block leaves the
# sensor a pure constant-bias source (the run is then identical to before this
# schema existed). The terms drive the three-axis strapdown mechanization through
# the IMU error model (IEEE Std 952-1997 §A.2; Groves 2013 §4.3). Scale-factor is
# in ppm; misalignment in rad (off-diagonal); g-sensitivity in (rad/s)/(m/s²);
# quantization in the sensor's output units; rate-ramp is a linear-in-time drift.
# [imu_classical.error_model]
# scale_gyro_ppm  = [1500.0, 1500.0, 1500.0]
# scale_accel_ppm = [1000.0, 1000.0, 1000.0]
# g_sensitivity   = [5.0e-5, 5.0e-5, 5.0e-5]
# rate_ramp_gyro  = [0.0, 1.0e-6, 0.0]
# quant_gyro      = [1.0e-5, 1.0e-5, 1.0e-5]

# each visible satellite's pseudorange:

planes = 6

phasing_f = 1.0

gps-denied-gravity-nav.toml:
# 60-minute GPS-denied gravity-map-matching benchmark (quantum alt-PNT).
#
# The validation-grade form of `gravity-map-nav.toml`: a vehicle flies a ~700 km track for
# a full one-hour GNSS outage, its inertial solution drifting to ≈ 70 km of position error.
# A cold-atom gravimeter samples the gravity anomaly along the track (with its real, seeded
# white-noise floor injected), and a hierarchical coarse-to-fine particle/grid matcher
# recovers the constant INS drift to a few hundred metres — the < 500 m GPS-denied target
# of ESA NAVISP's "Quantum Wayfarer" gravity-aided navigation.
#
# Consumed by `kshana::gravimeter::run_gps_denied_gravity_nav` (and its unit tests). The
# reference field is a low-degree spherical-harmonic trend plus synthetic mascons; Kshana
# does not bundle the full EGM2008 coefficient set, and a Monte-Carlo over map-representation
# error realisations is a documented follow-on (see docs/CAPABILITY.md).

# Dispatched by the scenario engine as `kind = "gravity-map"` (also consumed directly by
# `run_gps_denied_gravity_nav` in the unit tests, which ignore this field).
kind = "gravity-map"

# Maximum spherical-harmonic degree/order of the reference field.
nmax = 3

# Track flown GPS-denied: 90 waypoints, 40 s gravimeter averaging each ⇒ 3600 s = 60 min.
# An oblique leg keeps the scalar gravimeter sequence observable in both north and east.
start_lat_deg = 10.0
start_lon_deg = 20.0
step_lat_deg = 0.06
step_lon_deg = 0.045
waypoints = 90

# True constant INS position drift accumulated over the one-hour outage (≈ 70 km at ~13° lat,
# i.e. far past the 10 km the matched solution must beat).
drift_lat_deg = 0.5
drift_lon_deg = -0.4

# Cold-atom gravimeter: 1e-7 m/s²/√Hz ASD (≈10 µGal/√Hz), 40 s averaging ⇒ σ ≈ 1.6e-3 mGal.
gravimeter_asd = 1.0e-7
averaging_time_s = 40.0

# Map/representation error (mGal): combined with the sensor white noise into the matching σ.
map_sigma_mgal = 2.0

# Hierarchical offset search: ±0.8° at 0.08° to start, then three coarse-to-fine stages each
# shrinking the window and step 8× ⇒ final offset resolution 0.08° / 8² ≈ 140 m.
search_half_deg = 0.8
search_step_deg = 0.08
refine_stages = 3
refine_factor = 8.0
noise_seed = 1

# Low-degree anomalous, fully-normalised coefficients (the always-on regional trend).
[[coeffs]]
n = 2
m = 0
cbar = 6.0e-6
sbar = 0.0

[[coeffs]]
n = 3
m = 1
cbar = 3.0e-6
sbar = 2.0e-6

# Localized Gaussian anomalies (mascons) the track crosses — the distinctive high-degree
# features that make the constant drift observable.
[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 11.0
lon_deg = 20.8
amp_mgal = 45.0
sigma_deg = 0.30

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 12.4
lon_deg = 21.9
amp_mgal = -38.0
sigma_deg = 0.28

[[mascons]]
lat_deg = 13.8
lon_deg = 23.0
amp_mgal = 50.0
sigma_deg = 0.32

# Quantum gravity-map-matching navigation scenario (GPS-denied alt-PNT).
#
# Targets ESA NAVISP "Quantum Wayfarer" / QT-CCI gravity-map-matching vocabulary: a
# vehicle with an inertial unit and a cold-atom-interferometer gravimeter navigates with

[[mascons]]

hybrid-optical-rf.toml:
# Heterogeneous optical + RF PNT joint availability / precision / integrity (P5).
#
# Composes the Phase-7 pieces into one end-to-end analysis:
#   * L26 optical link budget  -> photon-limited two-way ranging CRLB + diffraction footprint
#   * L22 cross-modality RAIM   -> position AND timing protection level (loose RF x tight optical)
#   * L24 optical availability  -> N-station clear-sky diversity (independent + correlated union)
#   * L23 optical<->RF handoff  -> proven bit-continuous (no-jump) mean + NEES chi-square gate
#   * L25 joint FoM             -> P(available AND precision-grade AND integrity-assured)
#
# MODELLED. Validated closed forms: ranging CRLB (sigma_tau/sqrt(N)), diffraction footprint
# (lambda/D * range), chi-square protection-level quantile, union combinatorics, handoff
# mean-continuity + NEES gate, and the joint independent product. The loss allocations,
# sigma magnitudes, cloud-climatology inputs, correlations and P_HMI budget are Modelled
# representative inputs. Every field below is optional and shown at its default.
kind = "hybrid-optical-rf"

# --- L26 optical (1550 nm) two-way link budget ---
wavelength_nm      = 1550.0     # telecom C-band, eye-safe, low atmospheric loss
tx_power_w         = 1.0e-3     # 1 mW mean optical power (photon-starved lunar regime)
tx_aperture_m      = 0.85       # -> ~0.7 km diffraction footprint at lunar range (lambda/D)
rx_aperture_m      = 0.85
range_km           = 384000.0   # mean Earth-Moon distance
pulse_rms_ps       = 50.0       # signal-pulse RMS temporal width
integration_s      = 1.0
atmospheric_loss_db = 3.0       # Modelled 1550 nm clear-sky allocation
pointing_loss_db    = 3.0       # Modelled terminal pointing/jitter allocation
optics_efficiency   = 0.5       # Modelled
detector_efficiency = 0.7       # Modelled
two_way             = true      # round-trip ranging: range = c*dt/2, double-pass geometry

# --- RF (loose) reference solution ---
rf_pos_sigma_m      = 1.0       # horizontal 1-sigma
rf_vertical_sigma_m = 1.5       # vertical 1-sigma (vertical dilution)
rf_clock_sigma_s    = 3.0e-9    # 3 ns clock 1-sigma

# --- L22 cross-modality RAIM ---
p_fa              = 1.0e-5
p_md              = 1.0e-3
alert_limit_h_m   = 10.0
alert_limit_v_m   = 15.0
alert_limit_t_s   = 20.0e-9

# --- precision grade (the high-grade service the FoM scores) ---
grade_pos_m  = 0.1              # 10 cm position grade
grade_time_s = 1.0e-9           # 1 ns timing grade

# --- L24 optical ground-network availability ---
n_optical_sites  = 5
site_correlation = 0.15         # representative modest spatial (weather) correlation

# --- L25 joint FoM + L23 handoff ---
fom_correlation   = 0.5         # positive co-occurrence of the three P5 conditions
handoff_inflation = 0.2         # modality-transition covariance inflation at the switch
p_hmi             = 1.0e-7      # integrity-risk budget

# --- G15 bias / ramp fault injection against the cross-modality monitor ---
# The minimum detectable bias and the detection-power curve are ANALYTIC (non-central
# chi-square inversion), so they need no inputs of their own. These two only set the ramp
# rate the reported time-to-detect is a rate conversion of. Both MODELLED.
fault_ramp_rate_pos_m_s   = 0.05      # position-axis bias growth (m/s)
fault_ramp_rate_clock_s_s = 1.0e-11   # clock-axis bias growth (s/s)

# --- G17 post-handover coast: process noise and the alert-limit crossing ---
# Random walk on the existing 4-state (east, north, up, clock) handoff filter. The alert
# limits are the ones already declared above; only the process noise and the coverage
# factor are new. Both PSDs are MODELLED representative inputs and the crossing times

#   x = [ p(3) | v(3) | psi(3) | b_a(3) | b_g(3) | b  d ]

#     short-term inertial solution.

#     q-parameter clock engine (clock_state::q_from_allan) from the Allan profile below.
#
# The platform is GNSS-aided for a 100 s lead-in (the filter learns the biases, velocity and
# clock), then coasts through a 120 s GNSS outage on the CAI IMU + clock alone.
#

# INS/TRN coasting error model — position error against coast duration, and the coast
# durations at which it crosses 10 m and 50 m.
#
# The question this answers: when a GNSS (or aperture-duty-cycled) study says "assume a
# dead-reckoning drift of 0.001–0.050 m/s", where does that number come from? It comes
# from the IMU, and this scenario computes it instead of sweeping it. Five growth terms —
# accelerometer bias (t^2), gyro-bias tilt through gravity (t^3), velocity random walk
# (t^1.5), angle random walk (t^2.5) and scale factor times the travelled distance — are
# combined under a stated rule, and the threshold crossings are located by bisection on
# the combined model. Every crossing carries the per-contribution breakdown that says
# which error source put it there.
#
# Consumed by `kshana::inertial::coast` and dispatched as `kind = "ins-trn-coast"`. The
# growth laws are cross-checked against the engine's own stochastic dead-reckoner
# (`inertial::AccelModel`, Monte-Carlo) and its IMU error model
# (`inertial::imu_errors::ImuErrorModel`, double-integrated); the IMU class coefficients
# are representative Groves-Table-4.1-band figures, NOT a datasheet for any part.
kind = "ins-trn-coast"

# Representative IMU class: navigation, tactical, industrial or consumer. Any individual
# coefficient below can be overridden, which relabels the reported grade as `custom`.
imu_grade = "navigation"

# Airborne cruise. The scale-factor error mis-scales the TRAVELLED DISTANCE, so the speed
# is part of the error model, not decoration: at 250 m/s a 100 ppm scale factor is a
# 0.025 m/s floor on the mean drift rate that no coast duration falls below.
speed_m_s = 250.0
ref_accel_m_s2 = 0.0

# How the five contributions combine into one number. A MODELLING CHOICE, stated: `rss`
# reads each coefficient as a 1-sigma spec, `linear-sum` is the coherent worst case, and
# `det-sum-stoch-rss` adds the systematic terms while root-sum-squaring the independently
# driven random walks. All three are reported in `combination_sensitivity` either way.
combination = "rss"

# The crossings to report (m). These are inputs: the 10 m / 50 m pair is the default, not
# a constant compiled into the model.
crossing_thresholds_m = [10.0, 50.0]

# The drift-rate band a duty-cycle study sweeps (m/s), checked against per grade.
drift_band_lo_m_per_s = 0.001
drift_band_hi_m_per_s = 0.050

# Terrain-referenced aiding. TRN in this engine (`altpnt::terrain`, `altpnt::sequential`)

# RF jamming: a ground-based broadband jammer denying GNSS to a nearby receiver.

# The chain (Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS, 3rd ed. §9.4): the jammer's

lunar-beacon.toml:
# Surface-beacon augmentation of a lunar orbital navigation service.
#
# A south-polar lunar user sees a sparse orbital constellation inside a narrow, slowly
# moving patch of sky. Every line of sight points into roughly the same direction, so the
# ranging design matrix is ill-conditioned and the dilution of precision is large — the
# geometry problem, not a signal-power problem. A handful of SURVEYED SURFACE BEACONS fix
# it cheaply: a beacon near the local horizon contributes the low-elevation, wide-azimuth
# line-of-sight rows an all-overhead orbital set structurally cannot supply, and the
# horizontal DOP collapses.
#
# This run reports three configurations at one epoch, so the two routes to usable geometry
# can be compared directly:
#
#   * the satellites alone,
#   * the satellites plus whichever beacons clear the horizon, and
#   * a larger constellation instead — the expensive alternative to the same end.
#
# Each row carries its visible-source counts, its full DOP, and the realised 1-sigma
# accuracy in METRES. That last step is the point: a bare "PDOP 1.6" is dimensionless and
# easy to over-read, so the report multiplies it through a per-beacon user-equivalent
# ranging error (the root-sum-square of the clock-synchronisation, multipath and survey
# terms below) and states the answer as a distance.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS

# closed form (no atmosphere, so there is no refractive extension and the bound is exact);

lunar-differential-pnt.toml:
# Lunar DIFFERENTIAL PNT — a lunar DGNSS / SBAS analogue.
#
# A NovaMoon-class reference station at a KNOWN selenographic location computes
# per-satellite differential corrections from an ILLUSTRATIVE Moonlight / LCNS-class
# constellation; a roving user offset from it by baseline_km applies those corrections so
# the COMMON-MODE broadcast-ephemeris errors (orbit + clock) cancel.
#
# THE IDENTITY (what src/lunar_dpnt.rs implements):
#   ref_error_i      = -e_i . u_ref_i  + c_i           (the correction the station broadcasts)
#   user_raw_i       = -e_i . u_user_i + c_i
#   corrected_user_i = user_raw_i - correction_i = -e_i . (u_user_i - u_ref_i)
# The clock term c_i CANCELS EXACTLY (it is identical in both observations); the orbit
# term collapses to the projection onto the DIFFERENCE of the two line-of-sight unit
# vectors, which -> 0 as the baseline -> 0 (the spatial-decorrelation floor) and grows
# ~linearly with baseline. Mapping the corrected per-satellite range errors through the
# user geometry (a weighted-least-squares snapshot solve) gives the user POSITION error.
#
# NovaMoon is referenced only as a system CLASS (a public description of a lunar reference
# station); the constellation reuses the illustrative public-source LCNS-class set. These
# are illustrative parameters for exercising the differential method, NOT a real ephemeris,
# and imply NO affiliation, endorsement, heritage, certification or TRL.
#
# HONESTY: MODELLED. The common-mode cancellation is an EXACT algebraic identity; the
# spatial-decorrelation residual is a FIRST-ORDER geometric model (the LOS-difference
# projection of an injected orbit error), not a fitted decorrelation model from real lunar
# tracking. The user protection level REUSES the DO-229E SBAS protection-level machinery
# (crate::sbas) with the differential residual sigma as the per-satellite error budget.
# Deterministic given the seed. No real-data validation; no TRL/heritage/agency endorsement.
kind = "lunar-differential-pnt"

# Illustrative LCNS-class constellation (public-source approximation; not affiliated).
n_sats = 8
sma_km = 9737.4        # ~8000 km perilune altitude above the mean lunar radius
eccentricity = 0.6
inc_deg = 57.7
argp_deg = 90.0        # apolune over the southern hemisphere (south-pole favouring)

# NovaMoon-class reference station at a known south-polar selenographic location.
ref_lat_deg = -89.0
ref_lon_deg = 0.0

# User offset from the reference station along the surface (the baseline).
baseline_km = 50.0

# Injected COMMON-MODE per-satellite broadcast errors (the errors the correction removes).
orbit_err_m = 100.0    # orbit-error vector magnitude (random direction per satellite)
clock_err_m = 30.0     # clock error in range units (random sign per satellite)
noise_m = 0.0          # per-receiver measurement noise (0 => exact cancellation at 0 baseline)

seed = 42
t_s = 0.0              # epoch (seconds past the MCI/MCMF-aligned epoch)

# Differential residual sigma fed to the SBAS DO-229E protection-level reuse.
residual_sigma_m = 5.0
p_hmi = 1e-4           # integrity-risk budget (interface parity; DO-229E K-factors fixed)

# ── THE CORRECTION LINK ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The identity above assumes a PERFECT correction: computed by a station that knows
# exactly where it stands, delivered instantly, at infinite resolution. None of the three
# holds, and the three inputs below model what each costs. They feed the `correction_link`
# block of the result document ONLY -- with all three at the values written here, every
# number this scenario emitted before they existed is bit-for-bit unchanged.
#
# 1. SURVEY ERROR. The station forms its correction against the coordinate it BELIEVES.
#    An error there rides on every correction it broadcasts and reaches the user as
#    -delta . u_ref -- which contains no user geometry at all, so unlike the orbit term it
#    neither vanishes at zero baseline nor grows with baseline, and it transfers about
#    one-for-one into the user's position. Default 0.30 m is the crate's own lunar
#    reference-frame position-realisation allocation (lunar_time_budget frame_pos_error_m),
#    itself MODELLED: no lunar surface station has a published surveyed accuracy.
survey_sigma_m = 0.30      # reference-station 3-D coordinate 1-sigma (m), isotropic

# 2. CORRECTION AGEING. A correction computed at t and applied at t+tau is stale two ways.
#    Orbit: the satellite has MOVED, so the frozen orbit-error vector now projects onto a
#    rotated line of sight; the rotation comes from this crate's own propagator, so no
#    orbit-error rate is assumed anywhere. Clock: the satellite clock has drifted by
#    c*sigma_y(tau)*tau for the full-RAFS power law in crate::clock_specs, calibrated there
#    to a published one-day spec row. ILLUSTRATIVE default -- no lunar correction link has
#    a published latency -- which is why the report also emits a 0-300 s latency curve.
latency_s = 10.0           # age of the correction when the user applies it (s)

# 3. QUANTIZATION. The correction crosses a finite-rate link. The quantizer range is NOT a
#    free parameter: it is +/-(orbit_err_m + clock_err_m), an exact bound on the correction
#    magnitude for the injected error model, so the step is 2*(100+30)/2^bits = 1.0156 m at
#    8 bits and the residual variance is the uniform quantizer's step^2/12. The bit count
#    itself is an ILLUSTRATIVE input; 0 disables the term.
quantization_bits = 8      # bits per transmitted correction
lunar-frame-campaign.toml:
# Seven-parameter Helmert lunar frame datum driven by a SIMULATED OBSERVING CAMPAIGN (G9).
#
# The lunar-frame-realisation scenario injects a known similarity transform and recovers
# it — a solver unit test wearing the clothes of a result. This kind removes the planted
# answer: a network of Earth stations observes a catalogue of lunar-surface beacons over an
# explicit schedule, the lunar-VLBI delay partials are accumulated over that schedule into
# a beacon-coordinate Fisher information matrix exactly as lunar-vlbi-fim does, and that
# information is propagated through the Helmert design A = [I3 | [p]_x | p] at the
# catalogue points into the datum covariance H = A^T M_b A.
#
# Nothing is recovered from a planted transform, so the reported datum accuracy derives
# from the observing programme: halving the delay sigma halves it exactly, and lengthening
# the arc improves it because the libration the report MEASURES
# (sub_earth_direction_sweep_deg) is what separates the line-of-sight beacon coordinate
# from the plane-of-sky ones.
#
# Beacon-error correlation is MEASURED, not assumed. With the stations held fixed no
# observation touches two beacons, so the information matrix is exactly block-diagonal
# (offblock_fraction 0); with the stations estimated the Schur-marginalised block is
# coupled, the induced correlation is printed, and the whole propagation is re-run with it
# discarded so the price of an independence assumption is a number rather than a claim.
#
# The same propagation under an isotropic per-coordinate sigma, and the recovery error the
# lunar-frame-realisation scenario reports, are both run here and printed beside the
# campaign value with their ratios.
#
# MODELLED: the beacon catalogue is sourced but the CAMPAIGN is simulated — the station
# network and the delay sigma are illustrative inputs, individual delay observations are
# treated as independent, and the Moon-centre ephemeris, station clocks, troposphere and
# Earth-orientation parameters are held FIXED. Not a geodetic product.

kind = "lunar-frame-campaign"
lunar-frame-realisation.toml:
# Lunar reference-frame realisation — a 7-parameter Helmert (similarity) datum fit.
#
# Where src/lunar_frame.rs APPLIES the IAU 2015 WGCCRE lunar body orientation (a forward model),
# src/lunar_frame_realise.rs ESTIMATES (realises) a lunar reference frame from a network of point
# coordinates tied to a datum. The estimation core is a classic 7-parameter similarity transform
# mapping points p_i (estimated frame) to q_i (datum frame):
#
#     q_i = t + (1 + s) * R(theta) * p_i
#
# with translation t (m), scale s (dimensionless, ~1e-6 level) and the small rotation
# R(theta) = rz(theta_z) * ry(theta_y) * rx(theta_x). The seven parameters
# [tx, ty, tz, theta_x, theta_y, theta_z, s] are estimated from >= 3 non-collinear point pairs by
# weighted least squares via crate::batch_ls::gauss_newton (forward model flattens every q_i over
# all three components; weights = 1/sigma^2; x0 = zeros). A small orientation tie expresses the
# realised small rotation about the ICRF axes (relative to the IAU body orientation).
#
# THIS SCENARIO injects a KNOWN small Helmert transform (translation ~tens of m, rotation ~uradian,
# scale ~1e-7) into a well-spread synthetic point network (varied selenographic lat/lon mapped to
# MCMF, some points at altitude), adds seeded Gaussian noise, recovers the datum with helmert_fit,
# and reports the recovered transform, the per-parameter recovery error vs the injected truth, and
# the post-fit RMS residual.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED self-consistency. The oracle is the recovery of an injected 7-parameter
# similarity transform (noiseless to ~machine precision) plus the algebraic round-trip identity of
# apply_helmert. This is NOT a realisation of the lunar reference frame against real tracking / VLBI
# data and claims no absolute frame accuracy. Deterministic (seeded). No TRL, flight heritage or
# agency endorsement is claimed.
kind = "lunar-frame-realisation"

# Number of well-spread selenographic network points (>= 3).
n_points = 8

# Injected (truth) translation (m).
tx_m = 25.0
ty_m = -40.0
tz_m = 15.0

# Injected (truth) small rotation (micro-radians).
rot_x_urad = 3.0
rot_y_urad = -2.0
rot_z_urad = 5.0

# Injected (truth) scale (parts-per-billion; 100 ppb = 1e-7).
scale_ppb = 100.0

# Per-coordinate measurement noise standard deviation (m); weights = 1/sigma^2.
noise_sigma_m = 1.0

# Deterministic seed (measurement noise).
seed = 42

# Epoch (UTC) for the ICRF orientation tie.
epoch_year = 2024
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
lunar-interop-export.toml:

#
# Exports the lunar reference frame, the lunar time scale and a lunar ephemeris in
# CCSDS-based interchange forms, with round-trip / field conformance as the oracle.
#
# WHAT src/lunar_interop.rs does:
#   * export_lunar_oem  — REUSES the crate's CCSDS OEM 2.0 emitter (crate::oem),
#     re-tagged for the lunar context: REF_FRAME = the IAU 2015 WGCCRE lunar body

#     id, secular rate µs/day from crate::lunar_time, the published 56-59 µs/day band,

#   * export_kif_lunar — wraps the OEM + time descriptor + frame label in the existing
#     KIF envelope (crate::interchange) with the MODELLED honesty label.
#   * oem_conformance — checks the required CCSDS/LunaNet header fields are present, the
#     REF_FRAME/TIME_SYSTEM carry the expected lunar tokens, the META_START..META_STOP
#     framing and the position+velocity data lines are well-formed.
#
# HONESTY: MODELLED. The field NAMES and units are aligned with PUBLIC standards
# (CCSDS 502.0-B OEM, IAU WGCCRE 2015 lunar frames, LunaNet Interoperability
# Specification / IOAG lunar architecture). The deterministic round-trip and the

kind = "lunar-interop-export"

# Lunar body frame: MOON_ME (mean-Earth / polar-axis) or MOON_PA (principal-axis).

# Lunar time scale tag: LTC (Lunar Coordinate Time), TCL or UTC (the Earth tie).

# Sample ephemeris grid.
n_states = 9
step_min = 30.0

# Informational epoch label (the OEM grid hangs off a fixed deterministic epoch).

# Object name written to the OEM OBJECT_NAME / OBJECT_ID.

lunar-jamming.toml:
# Lunar-native RF jamming: per-satellite J/S for a lunar surface user.
#
# The `jamming` kind is Earth-shaped — it takes a Walker/SGP4 shell and a WGS-84
# geodetic receiver, so a lunar case could only be assembled outside the engine by
# running `link-budget` twice (once for the jammer leg, once for the satellite leg)
# and subtracting the two received powers by hand. This kind runs that subtraction
# inside the engine, per satellite, per epoch.
#
# It composes, and re-derives nothing:
#   * jamming::j_over_s_db, effective_cn0_dbhz, rx_antenna_gain_db, lock_status,
#     q_factor, nominal_cn0_dbhz, free_space_path_loss_db  (the interference chain),
#   * lunar_service::LunarConstellation + topocentric, lunar::selenographic_to_mcmf
#     (the lunar sky geometry: MCI -> MCMF, then az / el / slant range from a
#     selenographic surface user).
#
# Unlike the Earth kind, the signal leg is not a fixed received power: each
# satellite's isotropic received power is its own link budget,
# `sat_eirp_dbw - FSPL(slant range, carrier)`, so the J/S moves satellite by
# satellite with lunar range and elevation. The result is a TABLE — one row per
# visible (epoch, satellite) link — published as JSON and as `*.table.csv`. The
# aggregate figures of merit sit beside that table, never in place of it.
#
# Every field below is optional; the values shown are the defaults except for the
# jammer block. Run it with:  kshana scenarios/lunar-jamming.toml
#
# MODELLED. The constellation is the illustrative, public-source Moonlight/LCNS-class
# geometry (not the real ephemeris; no affiliation or endorsement implied), and the
# interference model is a link budget: no terrain shadowing of the jammer (a
# first-order effect in south-polar terrain), no multipath, no AGC near/far dynamics,
# no adaptive nulling, no acquisition-vs-tracking hysteresis.

kind = "lunar-jamming"

# --- constellation (illustrative LCNS-class; apolune over the south) ------------
n_sats = 4
sma_km = 9737.4          # R_moon + 8000 km
eccentricity = 0.6
inc_deg = 57.7
argp_deg = 90.0

# --- surface user (selenographic) ----------------------------------------------
site_lat_deg = -89.67    # Shackleton crater rim
site_lon_deg = 129.78
site_alt_m = 0.0

# --- epoch grid ------------------------------------------------------------------
horizon_hours = 12.0
step_min = 60.0
elev_mask_deg = 5.0

# --- signal leg (link-budget leg 2, evaluated per satellite) ---------------------
sat_eirp_dbw = 26.0            # representative lunar AFS EIRP
carrier_hz = 2.4e9             # S-band AFS carrier
chip_rate_hz = 1.023e6         # despreading processing gain
user_boresight_gain_dbi = 3.0  # J/S is invariant to this; it moves C/N0 only

# --- receiver ---------------------------------------------------------------------
temp_k = 290.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0
degraded_margin_db = 6.0

# --- jammer (link-budget leg 1). Omit this whole block for a clean-sky baseline. --
# Placed directly by standoff here. Give `lat_deg` and `lon_deg` instead to place it
# selenographically, and its range and elevation come from the same lunar geometry
# the satellites use (on an airless body a distant surface jammer then lands below
# the local horizon, and the antenna pattern hands it the horizon gain).
#
# 25 km is chosen because it splits the table: part of the visible set holds on and
# part does not. A single median J/S over these rows classifies the whole set as
# lost, which is exactly the collapse this kind exists to avoid.
[jammer]
power_dbw = 10.0        # 10 W
gain_dbi = 0.0
range_m = 25000.0
el_deg = 0.0            # a surface jammer on the user's local horizon
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0
lunar-joint-od-clock.toml:
# Lunar joint multi-technique OD + clock determination (a SIMULATED network).
#
# A single-epoch (snapshot) batch least-squares fit (src/lunar_combination.rs, on top of
# crate::batch_ls::gauss_newton) that FUSES three observation techniques to recover, together:
#   * a lunar surface station's 3-D position (NovaMoon-class, MCI metres),
#   * a small lunar constellation's per-satellite positions (MCI metres), and
#   * every asset's clock offset (station + each satellite, seconds).
#
# The three techniques:
#   1. Earth-baseline geodetic VLBI delays to the lunar station treated as the VLBI beacon
#      (reusing src/lunar_vlbi.rs, in geocentric inertial) — these make the station's FULL
#      3-D position observable;
#   2. lunar-local station<->satellite ranges (MCI Euclidean distance + the differenced clock
#      term scaled by c) — these tie the satellite positions and clock differences;
#   3. inter-satellite ranges (same form) — these tie the constellation's relative geometry.
#
# THE HEADLINE HONEST RESULT: lunar-local ranging alone leaves the station's position weakly
# observed along one direction (the range-only solve is ill-conditioned and the recovered
# station 3-D error is large). Adding the Earth-baseline VLBI delays makes the station's full
# 3-D position observable, and the recovered station error collapses to the metre level. The
# report runs the solve WITH and WITHOUT the VLBI legs on the same seed/truth and reports the
# station-observability improvement factor.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED simulated closed-loop recovery. An injected truth is mapped to synthetic
# observables through the SAME geometry model the solver inverts, seeded Gaussian noise is added,
# and the estimator recovers the injected truth within the noise. The oracle is internal
# consistency (truth recovery + NEES covariance realism), NOT real-data validation. There is no
# force-model propagation inside the solver — the satellites are fixed, distinct, illustrative
# points on a representative lunar orbit. No TRL, flight heritage or agency endorsement claimed.
kind = "lunar-joint-od-clock"

# Network size.
n_sat = 3     # constellation satellites
n_earth = 6   # Earth ground stations (more stations -> more independent VLBI baselines and
              # better Earth->sat radiometric multilateration geometry)

# Deterministic seed (measurement noise + truth jitter).
seed = 42

# Per-observable measurement noise standard deviations (weights = 1/sigma^2). Illustrative,
# representative of the modelled class (geodetic VLBI, coherent two-way + optical ISL ranging).
sigma_vlbi_s = 1.0e-11   # VLBI delay sigma (s) ~ 3 mm path length
sigma_range_m = 0.1      # radiometric / lunar-local range sigma (m)
sigma_isl_m = 0.1        # inter-satellite (optical) range sigma (m)

# Lunar surface station (south-polar NovaMoon-class site), selenographic.
station_lat_deg = -88.0
station_lon_deg = 23.0
station_alt_m = 0.0

# Representative constellation orbit radius (km, MCI) the illustrative fixed satellites sit on.
orbit_radius_km = 6000.0

# Snapshot epoch (UTC).
epoch_year = 2024
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
lunar-llr-datum.toml:
# Seven-parameter Helmert lunar frame datum from a REAL, ARCHIVED observing campaign (V3).
#
# Where lunar-frame-campaign removed the injected transform but still stated its station
# network, its schedule and its per-observation sigma as ILLUSTRATIVE inputs, this kind
# takes all three from measurement:
#
#   * the epochs are the ground-transmit times of archived ILRS Consolidated Laser Ranging
#     Data normal points;
#   * the observations are the laser ranges really fired at the five retroreflector arrays
#     on the Moon;
#   * every observation weight is that normal point's OWN archived precision,
#     bin_rms/sqrt(n_raw), read out of the file rather than assumed.
#
# Station coordinates come from the IERS ITRF2020 SLR solution propagated to epoch by their
# published velocities; reflector coordinates from JPL DE430 Table 7 in the
# mean-Earth/mean-rotation frame the IAU 2015 WGCCRE model realises.
#
# WHICH LINKS ARE MEASURED AND WHICH ARE MODELLED IS THE REPORT, NOT A FOOTNOTE. The
# Moon-centre ephemeris and the IAU body orientation stay modelled, and their combined size
# is emitted as the observed-minus-computed one-way range residual over every point used;
# troposphere, solid-body tides, station eccentricity, polar motion, UT1-UTC, relativistic
# delay and station clocks are absent and sit inside that residual. Because an ephemeris
# error reaches a covariance only through the DIRECTION of each line of sight, every run
# also re-solves the whole datum with all partials tilted by sensitivity_tilt_deg (sign
# alternating) and emits the ratio — so the covariance's insensitivity to the modelled
# ephemeris is a number, not an argument.
#
# Inter-array correlation is MEASURED at exactly zero rather than assumed, because a laser
# range touches one array. A record the catalogues cannot place — a station with no
# published ITRF position — is SKIPPED AND COUNTED, never given a substituted coordinate.
# The simulated campaign's own figures are RUN and printed beside the measured ones.
#
# MODELLED: the seven-parameter figures are a Cramer-Rao bound for a reduced parameter set
# on a real schedule. Not a solved datum, not an LLR analysis, not a geodetic product.
#
# DATA: the committed real-data slice ships with the repository but NOT with the published
# crate. From a repository checkout this file runs as written; from the crate, set
# data_dir to a copy of that slice.

kind = "lunar-llr-datum"
lunar-time-budget.toml:
# Coordinated Lunar Time (LTC) end-to-end time-error budget over a tau grid.
#
# A single averaging-time (tau) error table invites the objection "you picked the tau that
# flatters your clock." This scenario answers it: the seven LTC error terms are assembled as
# time-error curves x_i(tau) (seconds) across a whole grid of averaging times, root-summed into
# x_Sigma(tau), and the clock-vs-frame CROSSOVER tau is located — the tau at which the growing
# clock term overtakes the constant real-time frame-realisation term. Below the crossover the
# budget is frame-limited (the reference-frame realisation dominates, not the clock); above it the
# clock dominates. Where the crossover falls depends entirely on the clock class — for the default
# passive H-maser it is far out in tau, for a coarse mini-RAFS it is seconds — which is exactly why
# a single-tau number is misleading. (src/lunar_time_budget.rs)
#
# Honesty: MODELLED. The tau-slopes are closed-form and analytically checkable (clock tau^{+1/2}
# or tau^{+1}, floors tau^0, measurement tau^{-1/2}) and the clock rows reproduce the published
# one-day clock specs; but the RF/optical-link, frame-realisation, relativistic-residual and
# ephemeris floor MAGNITUDES are Modelled budget allocations (documented defaults, caller-
# overridable), not measurements. The contribution is the reproducible crossover tau, not a
# certified per-term number. Nothing here is certified for operational timekeeping.
kind = "lunar-time-budget"

# On-board clock class driving the (growing) clock term. One of:
#   optical-master | passive-h-maser | rafs | mini-rafs
clock = "passive-h-maser"

# The averaging-time (tau) grid is the default 1 s ... 1e7 s log-spaced grid (8 points/decade).
# Uncomment to override:
# tau_min_s = 1.0
# tau_max_s = 1.0e7
# points_per_decade = 8
lunar-time-offset.toml:
# Lunar coordinate time (LTC/TCL): the relativistic Earth-Moon clock rate.
#
# A clock on the lunar surface ticks faster than an Earth-geoid (TT) clock. A
# first-principles post-Newtonian identity (src/lunar_time.rs) sums two named terms:
#   - self-potential difference: the IAU L_G geoid potential (W0 = L_G*c^2) minus the
#     Moon's surface self-potential GM_moon/R_moon -> the dominant ~ +57.5 us/day; and
#   - kinetic (second-order Doppler): -<v^2>/2c^2 from the geocentric Moon velocity
#     (finite-differenced from the Montenbruck-Gill lunar series) -> ~ -0.5 us/day.
# The total secular rate ~ 57 us/day is reported with the published 56-59 us/day band.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED, not certified. The headline us/day figure is reference-dependent
# (Earth geoid W0 vs a lunar selenoid, the time-averaging window, neglected sub-us/day
# centrifugal/J2 corrections) -> a band, not a single number, is the honest output.
# Nothing here is validated to sub-nanosecond absolute accuracy or certified for
# operational timekeeping. The report also gives the accumulated LTC-TT offset over the
# horizon and supports an inverse-variance ensemble (a minimal lunar paper-clock).
kind = "lunar-time-offset"

epoch_year = 2000    # LTC origin epoch (UTC); rate varies < 1e-3 us/day over the J2000 era
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
horizon_days = 1.0   # accumulate the LTC-TT offset over one day (~57 us)
lunar-vlbi-fim.toml:
# Lunar-VLBI station-coordinate covariance from an explicit observing schedule (G8, paper D3).
#
# D3's published chain goes from a per-observation delay precision to a station coordinate
# uncertainty through an assumed ISOTROPIC equipartition factor g = 3. That step is the one
# the paper's own abstract calls modelled rather than measured. This scenario removes it:
# the lunar-VLBI delay partials are accumulated over a real schedule of (baseline x epoch)
# pairs into a Fisher information matrix, inverted, and reported as the station coordinate
# covariance — so the station sigma is an engine output.
#
# The state carries Earth-FIXED (ITRS) coordinates, so the Jacobian is the inertial partial
# rotated by each epoch's GCRS->ITRS matrix: Earth rotation is what makes those coordinates
# observable at all, and the report MEASURES the Earth-fixed line-of-sight sweep and the
# beacon declination rather than assuming them. One observation is one (baseline, epoch)
# pair with BOTH stations above the elevation mask, weighted 1/delay_sigma_s^2.
#
# What to read in the report
#   * per-station per-axis and 3-D sigmas — the computed answer;
#   * the equipartition value c*delay_sigma_s*sqrt(g/N) for the SAME schedule, printed
#     beside it with the ratio. That ratio IS the anisotropy the assumption discarded, and
#     the isotropic trace bound sqrt(p/trace(M)) makes AM-HM a hard floor, so the
#     assumption can only ever understate;
#   * rank, datum defect, condition number, the full spectrum and the free-network null
#     space, on every run. Under a rank deficiency the headline sigma is published NULL
#     with a status, never read out of a near-singular inverse;
#   * both baseline counts: delay closure tau_ik = tau_ij + tau_jk leaves only n-1 of the
#     n(n-1)/2 baselines geometrically independent.
#
# MODELLED: the Moon-centre ephemeris, station clocks, troposphere and Earth-orientation
# parameters are held FIXED and observations are treated as independent, so this is a
# Cramer-Rao bound for a reduced parameter set, not a predicted session result. The
# omitted differenced-Shapiro partial is measured by finite difference and emitted.
# Not a geodetic product.
#
# Every field below is the module default, written out so the run is reproducible from
# this file alone. Delete any line to fall back to the same value.

kind = "lunar-vlbi-fim"
lunar-vlbi.toml:
# Lunar geodetic VLBI: an Earth baseline observing a lunar-surface beacon.
#
# Two ground stations (a VLBI baseline, here a Goldstone-like and a Canberra-like site)
# observe a one-way signal from a NovaMoon-class transmitter on the lunar near side. The
# geodetic observable (src/lunar_vlbi.rs) is the NEAR-FIELD two-range difference
#   tau_geom = (|r2 - r_B| - |r1 - r_B|) / c
# (the Moon is near-field, not a plane wave), plus the station clock-offset difference and a
# differenced Earth-potential Shapiro term. The report gives the delay, its finite-difference
# rate, and the wavefront-curvature near-field correction over the pass, with partials
# available for OD/frame work.
#
# Oracle: in the far-field limit the geometric delay collapses to the same-codebase plane-wave
# delta-DOR observable (src/radiometric.rs), matched to machine precision; the partials are
# finite-difference checked. At true lunar distance the near-field correction is a non-zero
# tens-to-hundreds-of-microseconds term.
#
# Honesty: MODELLED, NOT validated against real VLBI data. Polar motion is dropped
# (xp = yp = 0) so station inertial positions carry a few-metre frame error; the beacon mixes
# a mean-equator-of-date Moon series with an ICRF body-fixed offset (jd_tdb ~ jd_tt), a
# frame-consistency mismatch below model fidelity; no light-time iteration, media or aberration
# beyond the differenced Shapiro. No TRL, flight heritage or agency endorsement is claimed.
kind = "lunar-vlbi"

# Station 1 (DSN Goldstone-like, California).
station1_lat_deg = 40.4256
station1_lon_deg = -116.8893
station1_alt_m = 1000.0

# Station 2 (DSN Canberra-like, Australia) — a long intercontinental baseline.
station2_lat_deg = -35.4014
station2_lon_deg = 148.9819
station2_alt_m = 688.0

# Beacon on the lunar near side (equatorial, sub-Earth point).
beacon_lat_deg = 0.0
beacon_lon_deg = 0.0
beacon_alt_m = 0.0

# Epoch (UTC) and pass sampling.
epoch_year = 2024
epoch_month = 1
epoch_day = 1
horizon_hours = 6.0
step_min = 30.0
maritime-port-approach-coast.toml:
# Maritime port approach with GNSS jammed: how long an inertial navigation system
# (INS) keeps a ship inside the harbour-approach accuracy budget once the Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) is lost.
#
# The mission question: a vessel fitted with an INS enters a harbour approach at
# 12 knots (6.17 m/s) when GNSS is jammed (see `maritime-strait-jamming.toml` for why).
# How many seconds of free-inertial coast does it have before its position error passes
# 10 m, and before it passes 100 m? Those are the two accuracy figures that
# International Maritime Organization (IMO) Resolution A.1046(27), on the World-Wide
# Radionavigation System, gives for harbour entrances and approaches (10 m, 95 %) and
# for ocean waters (100 m, 95 %). They are used here as budgets, not as a claim of
# compliance.
#
# The model is `ins-trn-coast`: five growth terms (accelerometer bias, gyro-bias tilt
# through gravity, velocity random walk, angle random walk and scale factor times the
# distance run), combined root-sum-square and searched for the crossing times. The IMU
# (inertial measurement unit) is the representative navigation-grade class from the
# engine's grade table (Groves 2013, Table 4.1 band), the class of INS fitted to naval
# and high-end offshore vessels. It is NOT a datasheet for any product. Change
# `imu_grade` to "tactical" or "industrial" to see how a cheaper unit shortens the coast.
#
# Honest scope: most merchant ships carry no INS; they dead-reckon on a gyrocompass and
# a speed log, which this engine does not model. No terrain or radar aiding is applied
# (`trn_fix_mode = "none"`), so this is the unaided coast. MODELLED: every figure is
# modelled from class coefficients, not measured on a vessel.
kind = "ins-trn-coast"

imu_grade = "navigation"

# 12 knots, a typical harbour-approach speed. The scale-factor term grows with the
# distance run, so speed is part of the error model.
speed_m_s = 6.17
ref_accel_m_s2 = 0.0

combination = "rss"

# IMO A.1046(27) harbour-approach and ocean-waters figures, used as budgets (m).
crossing_thresholds_m = [10.0, 100.0]

drift_band_lo_m_per_s = 0.001
drift_band_hi_m_per_s = 0.050

# No aiding: the free-inertial coast over the whole approach.
trn_fix_mode = "none"

# A one-hour approach and berthing window.
mission_duration_s = 3600.0
maritime-spoof-position-push.toml:
# Maritime GNSS spoofing: detecting a transmitter that drags a ship's reported position.
#
# The mission question: a spoofer near a shipping lane broadcasts counterfeit Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals slightly stronger than the real ones and
# pulls the ship's position fix several hundred metres off its true track. Position
# spoofing affecting ships has been publicly reported, for example vessels whose
# reported positions appeared on land; this file describes that pattern generically and
# models no particular incident. Would the receiver's own monitors catch it?
#
# The pack runs the combined spoof detector (`spoof-detect`): receiver autonomous
# integrity monitoring (RAIM) parity across satellites, automatic gain control (AGC)
# power monitoring and signal quality monitoring (SQM) of correlation distortion, fused
# into one decision. The attack is described in the parameters of the public TEXBAT test
# battery (Humphreys et al., ION GNSS 2012): the spoofer's power advantage, whether it
# is carrier-phase aligned, and whether it pushes position (a subset of satellites,
# visible to RAIM) or time.
#
# Here: a +2 dB power advantage (under the 3 dB AGC margin, so power alone misses it),
# not carrier aligned, pushing four satellites to drag the fix by 500 m. Try
# `carrier_aligned = true`, `push = "time"` and a smaller `power_advantage_db` to see
# the hard case that defeats these receiver-level layers.
#
# Honest scope: parameterised receiver observables, not raw signal samples; Kshana is a
# simulator, not a receiver. MODELLED: every figure is modelled, not validated against
# recorded maritime spoofing.

kind = "spoof-detect"

[attack]
power_advantage_db = 2.0
carrier_aligned = false
push = "position"
push_magnitude_m = 500.0
num_biased = 4
el_imbalance = 0.12

[detector]
sat_power_dbm = -130.0
agc_margin_db = 3.0
sqm_tolerance = 0.10
raim_p_fa = 1.0e-3
sigma_m = 5.0
fusion_threshold = 0.5
maritime-strait-jamming.toml:
# Maritime GNSS jamming: a shore- or vessel-borne broadband jammer denying the Global
# Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) to a ship crossing open water.
#
# The mission question a ship's navigator or a coastal authority asks: how far across
# the water does a modest jammer take GNSS away? Over the sea there is no terrain or
# clutter between the jammer and the ship's antenna, so free-space path loss is the
# only thing that weakens the jammer, and a low-power device reaches a long way.
# Widespread GNSS interference affecting shipping has been publicly reported in several
# sea areas; this file does not model any particular incident.
#
# The chain is the one in `jamming-demo.toml` (Kaplan & Hegarty, Understanding GPS/GNSS,
# 3rd ed., §9.4): jammer received power sets the jammer-to-signal ratio J/S, despreading
# and the spectral-separation factor turn it into an effective carrier-to-noise density
# C/N0 per satellite, and a satellite is lost below the 25 dB-Hz tracking threshold.
# Here a 50 W (17 dBW) broadband jammer on a 30 m mast sits 30 km from a ship at sea
# level. Free-space loss over 30 km at the L1 frequency (1575.42 MHz) is about 126 dB,
# which leaves a mean J/S of about 48 dB, well past the roughly 35 dB a coarse/acquisition (C/A)
# code tracking loop tolerates, so the receiver loses every satellite. Move the jammer
# out or cut its power to find the range at which tracking returns (J/S falls about
# 20 dB per decade of range).
#
# Assumptions: 0 dBi jammer and ship antennas toward each other (a ship's GNSS antenna
# is not a controlled-reception pattern antenna (CRPA)), free-space propagation with no
# sea-surface multipath, a GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell. The receiver position is
# a generic point in the northern Baltic Sea. MODELLED: every figure is modelled, not
# validated against measured maritime interference.
kind = "jamming"
seed = 1
mask_deg = 5.0
tracking_threshold_dbhz = 25.0

[time]
step_s = 30.0
duration_s = 1800.0

[receiver]
lat_deg = 59.80
lon_deg = 24.90
alt_m = 0.0

# A GPS-like 24-satellite Walker shell (6 planes x 4), propagated through the SGP4 core.
[constellation]
altitude_km = 20200.0
inclination_deg = 55.0
planes = 6
sats_per_plane = 4
phasing_f = 1.0

# 50 W broadband jammer on a 30 m mast, 30 km due east of the ship (ECEF, metres).
[jammer]
position_ecef_m = [2904623.523, 1381438.498, 5489328.347]
power_dbw = 17.0
gain_dbi = 0.0
jammer_type = "broadband"
bandwidth_mhz = 20.0
mars-pnt-lmo.toml:
# Mars PNT — Low-Mars-Orbit user navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay
# constellation (areostationary relays broadcasting one-way + relaying two-way to a
# deep-space station) through the joint one-way/two-way radiometric fusion estimator.
#
# Figures of merit are the estimator's FORMAL COVARIANCE bounds (1σ / 3σ position) and
# the achieved RMS vs a synthetic closed-loop truth — a simulated navigation FoM, NOT an

kind = "mars-pnt"

step_s = 60.0                # observation cadence

two_way_period_s = 1800.0    # a coherent two-way (clock-free, orbit-pinning) pass every 30 min

# Mars PNT — a fixed surface user (a lander / rover on the rotating Mars surface)
# navigated against the simulated MARCONI relay constellation through the joint

#
# A surface point is NOT in free-fall — it co-rotates rigidly with Mars (held up by the

user = "surface"             # fixed point on the equator at the prime meridian (co-rotating)
clock_class = "uso"

seed = 331514052

# Mars PNT — a Mars transfer / capture user (a high, eccentric areocentric arc — the
# long arc a vehicle flies on approach / in a capture orbit) navigated against the

kind = "mars-pnt"

user = "transfer"            # high eccentric capture-class arc (perigee ~500 km, apogee ~6 Rm)
clock_class = "dsac"         # a deep-space atomic clock (the most stable class)
